title: You built the life everyone applauded…
paragraphs:
You built the life everyone applauded…
so why does it still feel empty?

You don’t say it out loud.
But it whispers when you’re alone.
When the noise dies.
When the phone is down.

Worked hard.
Chased purpose.
Earned respect.
Maybe even served in church.
But something beneath the surface is cracking.
Here’s the tension most people avoid:

You can succeed publicly
…while starving eternally.

You can look fulfilled
…and still feel hollow.

You can build a life “under the sun”
and never realize you’ve left God out of it.

Wealth beyond imagination.
Wisdom that stunned nations.
Pleasure, power, influence.

If fulfillment could be purchased—
he would have owned it.
“Vanity of vanities… all is vanity.” — Ecclesiastes 1:2

It means vapor.
Smoke.
Something you can see… but never hold.
Life without God feels exactly like that.

Real—but empty.
Visible—but weightless.
Busy—but meaningless.
And here’s the detail most miss:
Life under the sun is life without eternal perspective.

It’s what happens when God is not the center—
even if He’s still somewhere in the picture.

Your achievements don’t satisfy.
Your relationships don’t complete you.
Your victories don’t last.

Because you were never designed
to be sustained by temporary things.
Then Solomon drops this truth like lightning:
“He has set eternity in the human heart…” — Ecclesiastes 3:11

That restlessness you feel?
That quiet dissatisfaction?
That constant reaching for “more”?

God placed eternity inside you—
so nothing temporary would ever fully satisfy you.
Your emptiness is not your enemy.
But here’s where it gets uncomfortable:
We try to fill it with sin.
We tell ourselves, “If I just get this… I’ll be okay.”

But every time we reach for something other than God—
we sink deeper into the same emptiness.
Because sin doesn’t solve the void.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
We weren’t just made for purpose.
We were made for God Himself.
And sin separated us from Him.
That’s why even the “best moments” feel incomplete.
The moment Ecclesiastes is quietly pointing toward.
The answer is not “find your passion.”
The answer is not “fix your life under the sun.”
Jesus didn’t come to decorate your empty life.
“I came that they may have life and have it abundantly.” — John 10:10
Here’s the Gospel, clear and unfiltered:

You and I have sinned.
We’ve built lives around ourselves instead of God.
We’ve chased things that cannot save us.
But God didn’t leave us there.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Into our brokenness.
Into our emptiness.
Into our sin.

The guilt.
The shame.
The striving.
The endless chasing.
Proving that life is not under the sun anymore.
You don’t need to fill the void.
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.” — Acts 3:19

Bring your emptiness.
Bring your questions.
Bring your hidden struggles.
Jesus is not waiting to condemn you.

A life where your worth isn’t based on performance.
Where your peace isn’t tied to circumstances.
Where your purpose isn’t temporary.
Are you tired of chasing what never satisfies?

Are you ready to stop living “under the sun”
and start living with God at the center?
“Jesus… I’m done running. I need You.”
If this spoke to you, don’t keep it to yourself.

From emptiness to eternity—
because Jesus fills what the world never could.
